target.title: refactor(sessions): trim private SQLite surface
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The SQLite session owner still exposed duplicate contract types, zero-caller transcript readers, and module-local helpers after the storage cutover. Those exports inflated the internal API and kept 28 known-unused entries in the enforced Knip baseline.

## Why This Change Was Made

Delete 16 dead declarations and helper implementations, make 14 live implementation details module-private, and remove their 28 baseline entries. The storage-neutral session accessor, Plugin SDK surface, active latest-assistant-text reader, SQLite persistence behavior, and test-only exports remain unchanged.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. Session internals have 175 fewer production lines and a narrower ownership boundary.

## Evidence

- Fresh codebase-memory graph: 305,758 nodes / 1,265,915 edges. The two removed readers had zero callers; the three privatized helpers had only same-module callers.
- Full live scan of all 2,811 open pull requests, including all file pages for 39 pull requests over 100 files: no semantic overlap with the changed session symbols or baseline entries.
- Public-surface audit found no candidate exports in package subpaths, Plugin SDK declarations, docs, dynamic imports, or tagged package maps.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxbwhptdpy8jcxcahypw0cd2`, run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29205702175:
  - `pnpm deadcode:exports`: baseline matched 5,978 entries.
  - 232/232 focused tests passed across eight session, transcript, search, persistence, checkpoint, and concurrency suites.
  - Path-scoped `pnpm check:changed` passed formatting, core/core-test typechecks, lint, import-cycle, database-first, SDK baseline, and repository guards.
- Fresh `gpt-5.6-sol` autoreview with medium reasoning: local diff clean at 0.95 confidence; rebased branch clean at 0.94 confidence.

AI-assisted: yes. No transcript attached per operator preference.
